title: Introducing Cursor Router
description: Auto mode is now powered by Cursor Router, an intelligent model router that analyzes each request by task type and complexity and sends it to the right model for the job. Users can select from three optimization modes: Intelligence (frontier quality matching the most powerful models), Balance (strong quality matching popular daily-driver frontier models), and Cost (optimizing token spend while reaching high available intelligence). Balance and Intelligence modes bill at the routed model's rate. Admin controls allow enabling the router per team/group, restricting optimization modes, setting defaults, and allowing or blocking specific underlying models. Available across desktop, web, iOS, CLI, and SDK. Enabled by default for Teams plans; Enterprise admins can activate via dashboard. Grok 4.5 is included as a price-efficient routing option. Early-access customers reported 30-50% savings on auto-routed requests versus running everything on Opus 4.8, with up to ~60% savings in some cases.

title: Doubled Usage Limits for All Individual and Teams Plans
description: Cursor announced that usage limits have been doubled (2x) for all individual and teams plans. The increased allowances apply to Grok, Composer, and any new Cursor models. The move was widely seen as a competitive response as rivals like Kimi K3, GitHub Copilot, and Windsurf escalate the AI coding arms race. Some coverage placed the paid-plan doubling a few days earlier (~July 16), suggesting a phased rollout across plans. There is ongoing community discussion about whether the 2x usage is a temporary promotion or a permanent change.

title: Agent Swarms and the New Model Economics
description: A research-focused blog post by Wilson Lin (17 min read) exploring the economics of multi-agent systems and model usage. The post analyzes how agent swarms -- teams of AI agents working collaboratively -- change the cost and efficiency calculus of AI-assisted development. It discusses new model economics in the context of routing, multi-agent orchestration, and the trade-offs between frontier model quality and cost optimization.

title: Improvements to Cursor in Slack
description: Cursor in Slack received significant upgrades. Interaction improvements: Cursor now responds with a plan before it begins work so users can redirect early. Status updates are provided as it works. In-message buttons were replaced with compact footer links; tables, PRs, and artifacts render more cleanly. Multi-Repo Environment Support: Cursor can start in a named multi-repo environment from Slack rather than a single default repo, with a 'Switch repository' button appearing mid-task when a different repo is needed. Cross-Channel Workflows: Cursor can now read from and send messages to other Slack channels and threads, pulling context from elsewhere in the workspace and posting updates to relevant threads or channels.

title: Grok 4.5 Model Card
description: Cursor published the official model card for Grok 4.5, the first jointly pretrained model from Cursor and SpaceXAI (xAI). Grok 4.5 is a mixture-of-experts model trained jointly with xAI, using trillions of tokens of Cursor data capturing coding and broader knowledge work patterns. Billed as their most intelligent model yet, it features a 500K context window and is positioned for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work. Grok 4.5 is included as a price-efficient routing option in Cursor Router.
